title: Return Premium Computation for a Sale Cancellation — Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)
content:
On an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** policy cancelled because the insured home was sold, the returned premium is computed as follows.

## Clause

The returned premium is the term premium times the unexpired days over the days from the term start to the term end, but never more than the term premium less the minimum earned share of it, rounded to the cent once at the end. The unexpired days are the days from the term start to the term end less the earned days. The earned days are the days from the term start to the date the cancellation takes effect, which is the sale closing date. The minimum earned share is the tier's minimum earned premium percentage. Where the paid claim with the latest date of loss on this policy has a date of loss on or after the term start and a net payment above zero after voided payments, nothing is returned.

The sale closing date is the cancellation effective date of the Tidemark HomeFlood policy (HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies) whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record, cancelled for the sale. The term premium, term start and term end are those on the excess policy record. The paid-claim bar is read on the paid claim with the latest date of loss on this policy: its net payment is all payments issued on that claim number less all payments voided on it, and the bar applies when that net is above 0. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

## Computation (hypothetical figures)

| Case | Term premium | Days of term | Earned days | Minimum earned share | Returned premium |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2000.00 | 365 | 100 | 25 percent | 2000.00 times 265 over 365, that is 1452.05; below the limit of 1500.00 |
| B | 2000.00 | 365 | 50 | 25 percent | 2000.00 times 315 over 365 is 1726.03, above 1500.00, so 1500.00 |
| C | as A, but the paid claim with the latest date of loss fell inside the term and still has a net payment above zero | | | | nothing |

If, in case C, every payment on that latest paid claim had been voided, its net payment would be zero and case A's figure would stand.
